title: Hardware Recovery of the Analytic Pauli-Transfer-Matrix Structure of One-Axis-Twisting Boundary Channels
description:
Theory, exact simulation, pre-registration, and three runs on IBM Quantum hardware (ibm_marrakesh) measuring the predicted Pauli-transfer-matrix element T_xx = A·cos^(N-2)(χt/2) of the one-axis-twisting (OAT) boundary-pair channel, including its exact null at χt = π.

Proved analytically from the closed-form boundary density matrix: T_zz = 0, T_yy = 0, and the T_xx form, with the corollary that phase-only (Rz) local corrections cannot exceed the classical fidelity bound of 2/3 for any N or coupling time.

Measured on hardware, across three pre-registered runs: a 12.5σ signed ordering across three points (Run 1); a nine-point sweep recovering the functional form at R² = 0.986 with the internal null resolved to 0.4σ using 4000 shots (Run 2); and a disjoint-layout replication at R² = 0.976 with the null at −0.12σ (Run 3), establishing layout independence.

Raw shot counts, readout-calibration matrices, pre-registration files, and IBM job IDs are archived for every run — the entire analysis reproduces from counts upward without IBM access.

Includes docs/DISCOVERY_NARRATIVE.md, a condensed narrative account of the research path that records the falsified conjectures (an X-state fidelity formula retracted after direct numerical optimization), a retracted scrambling claim traced to a truncation artifact, three wrong circuits caught in dry runs before consuming hardware time, and a deliberately descoped fourth run — alongside the results that survived.

Claim boundary: this is a hardware measurement of an analytically predicted two-body observable. It is not a demonstration of quantum teleportation, a teleportation-advantage claim, or a hardware-confirmed theorem.

Simulation phase supported by Google TPU Research Cloud; hardware phase by the IBM Quantum Open Plan.

Companion result: one budget. This repository and its sibling (relational-time-ibm-quantum) ran as independent programmes and measure the same law -- coherence surviving as a product of half-angle state overlaps, one factor per party that has acquired distinguishing information -- here against COUPLING ANGLE, there against TIME. Placed together, every correlation magnitude either programme measured turns out to be drawn on one conserved unit, spent twice over: between a subsystem's local coherence and its entanglement with a partner (Jakob-Bergou complementarity, Phys. Rev. A 68, 022107, 2003), and between its entanglement with one partner and with another (Coffman-Kundu-Wootters monogamy, Phys. Rev. A 61, 052306, 2000). Both totals are exactly 1 and depolarizing noise never pushes either above it. The consequence, which neither programme states alone: a Page-Wootters clock is a good clock in proportion to the entanglement it spends on its own system, so no correlation magnitude can serve as a shared temporal reference between two good clocks. The sibling measured both trade-offs as continuous hardware curves (r = -0.9573 within a pair; r = -0.9833 across two clocks, both endpoints reaching exactly zero). THIS repository's contribution to that argument is the separable state: at chi_t = pi the boundary state is I/4 -- maximally mixed marginals, concurrence exactly zero, SEPARABLE -- to pair against the sibling's maximally entangled d=2 null, which also has maximally mixed marginals. A marginal observable reads zero on both while the joint correlator T_xx separates them at 0 versus +1. Neither programme could make that contrast alone. This repository also supplies the first instance of the certification wall both programmes hit: entanglement is not identifiable from PTM anisotropy alone, resolved by V_Q over Haar-random settings. The identities are standard and attributed as such; the measured curves are the contribution.
notes: Simulation phase (exact boundary-state core, MPS automaton to N >= 64, Lindblad dephasing sweeps, and the recovery-geometry search) supported by Google TPU Research Cloud, grant window 2026-04-21 to 2026-06-21, extended one month. Hardware phase used the IBM Quantum Open Plan and no TRC resources.
